questions.stem: A 15-year-old girl was brought by her mother to the emergency department. The patient appeared cachexic and was unconscious. Her mother gave a history of fever with loose stools for 6 days which they managed just with paracetamol and the condition of the patient kept deteriorating. Her last CBC Complete blood count report showed leukopenia. The patient, unfortunately, succumbed to death. On autopsy, splenomegaly was revealed along with longitudinal ulcers observed in the intestine. What could be the possible diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Enteric fever
  • The given clinical scenario followed by the autopsy findings of longitudinal ulcers classically is a presentation of typhoid i.e. enteric fever.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 246

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man complains of a persistent high fever with chills, malaise, and diffuse abdominal pain for over a week. He recently returned from a trip to India. The fever began slowly and increased to 40.0°C (104.0°F) over the last 4 days. A physical exam reveals a white-coated tongue, enlarged spleen, and rose-coloured spots on the abdomen. A bone marrow aspirate was sent for a culture that revealed motile, gram-negative rods. Which of the following is true about the organism and the pathophysiology underlying this condition?

options.label: A
options.text: It forms blue-green colonies with a fruity odour

options.label: B
options.text: It survives intracellularly within phagocytes of Peyer's patches

options.label: C
options.text: Splenectomy may be necessary for carriers

questions.answerText: It survives intracellularly within phagocytes of Peyer's patches
questions.solutionHtml:
It survives intracellularly within phagocytes of Peyer's patches
  • This patient has typhoid fever (enteric fever), which is caused by Salmonella typhi, a motile gram-negative bacteria with peritrichous flagella. Salmonella has somatic O, capsular Vi, and flagellar H antigens. Typhoid fever presents as a gradual onset of high-grade fever over several days with relative bradycardia (Faget sign). Fever starts low and increases daily in a stepwise pattern. It is associated with generalized weakness, abdominal pain, constipation, and headaches. Some people develop rose-coloured spots on the abdomen. Diarrhoea and vomiting are uncommon. Untreated cases may lead to complications, including haemorrhage, intestinal perforation with resulting septicemia, and/or peritonitis, encephalitis, cholecystitis, and osteitis.
  • Some people may carry the bacterium within their gallbladder without being affected, termed as ‘carriers’; however, they are still able to spread the disease to others. Typhoid fever spreads by the faecal-oral route. Salmonella enters the host's system primarily through the distal ileum (Peyer's patches). The bacteria survive inside macrophages and co-opt the macrophages' cellular machinery for their own reproduction as they are carried through the mesenteric lymph nodes to the reticuloendothelial tissues of the liver, spleen, and bone marrow. Some bacteria infect the gallbladder and come back again to the gut within bile, either to reinfect Peyer's patches or to be shed in faeces to infect other people.
  • The diagnosis of typhoid fever is made by characteristic signs and symptoms along with observing Salmonella typhi in any blood, bone marrow, or stool cultures.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th Edition, Lange McGraw Hill Publications, Page No 315

questions.stem: All of the following are used in enteric fever except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Amikacin
  • Gentamicin and amikacin are aminoglycoside antibacterial agents that are mainly used for the treatment of extracellular pathogen infections, such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa and E. coli infections, and thus are not commonly used for the treatment of typhoid fever.
  • Other options B, C and D are used in enteric fever.
  • Commonly prescribed antibiotics include Ciprofloxacin (Cipro).
  • Azithromycin-.This may be used if a person is unable to take ciprofloxacin or the bacteria is resistant to ciprofloxacin. Ceftriaxone.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 240

questions.stem: What is the reservoir for Salmonella typhi?
questions.solutionHtml:
Humans
  • Salmonella Typhi (S. Typhi) are bacteria which infect the intestinal tract and the blood.
  • The disease is referred to as typhoid fever.
  • Paratyphi A, B and C bacteria cause a similar illness which is included under the typhoid heading.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 232

questions.stem: In a patient with typhoid, diagnosis after 15 days of the onset of fever is best done by:
questions.solutionHtml:
Widal
  • Typhoid fever, also known simply as typhoid, is a bacterial infection due to a specific type of Salmonella that causes symptoms.
  • Typhoid fever is a systemic infection caused by Salmonella Typhi, usually through ingestion of contaminated food or water.
  • Widal test in the diagnosis of typhoid fever. Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi bacteria cause typhoid fever.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology, 28th Edition, Page No. 741

questions.stem: In which of the following sites is Salmonella typhi most likely to be found during the carrier state?
questions.solutionHtml:
Gallbladder

Up to 10% of untreated patients become carriers.

  • Carriers are of two types:
  • Faecal carriers (more common): Multiply in the gallbladder and are excreted in fa
  • Urinary carriers: Multiplication takes place in kidneys and bacilli are excreted in urine.


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 298-301, 480, 488-89, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 404-407

questions.stem: A 4-year-old has a fever and diarrhoea. Blood culture grows a gram-negative rod. This is most likely to be which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Salmonella
  • Enterocolitis is the most common manifestation of Salmonella In the United States, S. typhimurium and S. enteritidis are prominent, but enterocolitis may be caused by more than 3000 strains of Salmonella.
  • Bacteraemia is rare (2-4%) except in immunodeficient persons, infants and elderlies.
  • Stool cultures may remain positive for Salmonella weeks after clinical recovery.


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 298-301, 480, 488-89, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 404-407

questions.stem: For paratyphoid fever, all are true except:

options.label: D
options.text: Milder disease as compared to typhoid fever

questions.solutionHtml:
Carrier state not seen
  • A carrier state can develop in both typhoid and paratyphoid fever.


Ananthnarayan 12th Edition, Page No. 298-301, 480, 488-89, Apurba S Sastry 3rd edition, Page No. 404-407
